method: Written from the catalog.json records of each province (titles, call numbers, edition and reading-log counts, access status) and the example reader's synthetic history. Every [OL…W] id is checked by scripts/prototypes/terra-incognita.mjs; counts are from this 7,127-work sample, not from the whole Library of Congress. Years are Open Library first-publication dates, which are crowd-edited and sometimes wrong.

guides.text:
## Lay of the land

The largest province on the Science continent: 1,458 call-numbered works in this sample but only 127 Gutenberg titles, so it is nearly all settlement and very little forest. Two towns dominate. QA71–90, instruments and machines, holds 563 works (the computing shelves); QA273–280, probabilities and mathematical statistics, holds 328. Algebra (QA150–272.5) and analysis (QA299.6–433) lie between them.

## Landmarks

The highest peaks are old: Euclid's Elements [OL912133W], with 175 editions, and Newton's Principia [OL104736W], with 104. In the statistics town the landmark textbooks are Feller's Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications [OL146759W] and Jaynes's Probability Theory [OL5911565W], both already flagged by this explorer.

## Free to forage

- Bayes, An Essay towards Solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances [OL14986078W]: public domain, about 113 pages
- Bickel and Doksum, Mathematical Statistics [OL6903525W]
- Whitehead and Russell, Principia Mathematica [OL1133702W]
- Thompson, Calculus Made Easy [OL1084219W]

## Rare sightings

Few readers have logged Dietrich's Uncertainty, Calibration, and Probability [OL4470333W] (no ebook) or Kadane's Rethinking the Foundations of Statistics [OL1992486W]. Raiffa's Applied Statistical Decision Theory [OL2620278W] sits at QA279.4 with four reading-log entries.

## For this explorer

Thirty-seven flags, most of them in QA273–280 and on the QA76 computing shelves. The nearest unclaimed ground is QA279.4–279.5, decision theory and Bayesian statistics: Raiffa is the obvious next landfall, and Bayes's own essay is a short, free read.

## Lay of the land

A small province with two halves. Q1–295 covers general science, its history and its philosophy (185 works); Q300–390, cybernetics (183 works), in practice means machine learning at Q325, artificial intelligence at Q334–336 and information theory at Q350–390.

## Landmarks

The peaks are early-modern and ancient: Locke's Essay Concerning Human Understanding [OL880201W], with 188 editions (this record shelves it at Q111), Descartes's Discours de la méthode [OL1151518W] and Aristotle's Physics [OL151632W]. On the cybernetics side the most-read landmark is Russell and Norvig's Artificial Intelligence [OL2896994W].

## Free to forage

- Poincaré, La science et l'hypothèse [OL708894W]
- Descartes, Discours de la méthode [OL1151518W]
- Aristotle, Physics [OL151632W]

## Rare sightings

Brillouin's Science and Information Theory [OL11309051W] and Devlin's Logic and Information [OL69553W] are rarely logged, though they sit where information theory meets epistemology. So is the early Machine Learning collection edited with Michalski [OL18297859W].

## For this explorer

Twenty-six flags, most of them in Q325–335 (machine learning and AI), plus The Black Swan [OL3295030W] at Q375. The gap is the philosophy-of-science shelf at Q175: Whitehead's The Concept of Nature [OL1133703W] is flagged, but Feyerabend's Against Method [OL455919W], which is borrowable, is still in the fog beside it.

## Lay of the land

Economic theory and demography: 414 works and 83 Gutenberg titles. The largest town is HB131–147, methodology (124 works), where econometrics and mathematical economics live. Welfare theory (HB846–846.8, 51 works) and economics as a science (HB71–74, 28) follow. Forecasting keeps an outpost at the far end of the province, at HB3730 among the business cycles.

## Landmarks

Three public-domain peaks: Marx's Das Kapital [OL628450W] (189 editions) and Mill's Principles of Political Economy [OL1068184W], both flagged by this explorer, and Smith's The Wealth of Nations [OL76827W], which is not. Among modern works, Heilbroner's The Worldly Philosophers [OL1847023W] has 67 editions.

## Free to forage

- Smith, The Wealth of Nations [OL76827W]
- Mansfield and Yohe, Microeconomics [OL1879080W]
- Osborne and Rubinstein, Models in Microeconomic Theory [OL26502258W], a 2020 textbook that Open Library marks as public

## Rare sightings

Molho's The Economics of Information [OL2624211W] and Hansen's Probability and Statistics for Economists [OL27091828W] have almost no reading-log entries, yet both sit squarely on this explorer's interests, in the methodology town.

## For this explorer

Twenty-five flags, from Superforecasting [OL18233878W] at HB3730 to a run of microeconomics textbooks at HB171–172. The behavioural-economics shelf at HB74 is half explored: Freakonomics [OL278022W] is flagged, but Nudge [OL3936258W] and Predictably Irrational [OL9302660W] are still in the fog.

## Lay of the land

Psychology: 398 works and 447 Gutenberg titles, so BF is half settlement and half forest. Its capital town is BF309–499, consciousness and cognition (190 works), which holds judgment and decision making at BF441–448. Applied psychology (BF636–637) and developmental psychology (BF712–724.85) come next.

## Landmarks

By editions the peaks are popular rather than scientific: James Allen's As a Man Thinketh [OL43024W] (658 editions) and Carnegie's How to Win Friends and Influence People [OL1063267W]. One odd specimen: Open Library files Herodotus's Histories [OL15678068W] here, at BF121.

## Free to forage

- Darwin, The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals [OL515301W]
- Russell, The Analysis of Mind [OL1088578W]
- Dewey, Human Nature and Conduct [OL111293W]

## Rare sightings

Simon's Models of Thought [OL1205036W] (borrowable, three reading-log entries) and Broadbent's Perception and Communication [OL5258506W] are founding texts of cognitive psychology that almost nobody in this catalog has logged.

## For this explorer

Twelve flags, nine of them packed into BF441–448: Thinking, Fast and Slow [OL15992072W], Rational Choice in an Uncertain World [OL5595682W] and Farsighted [OL19749391W] among them. The rest of the province is fog. Simon is the natural bridge from judgment research to the cognition shelves around it.

## Lay of the land

Speculative philosophy: 135 works. Ontology (BD300–450, 79 works) is the biggest town. Epistemology (BD143–237, 39 works) is the one that matters for a forecaster: theories of knowledge, truth and evidence. Cosmology (BD493–701) is small and includes causation.

## Landmarks

By editions the first peak is Greene's The 48 Laws of Power [OL1968368W], which this catalog shelves at BD438. The philosophical landmarks are Popper's Conjectures and Refutations [OL1984581W] (44 editions) and Heidegger's Introduction to Metaphysics [OL77595W].

## Free to forage

- Reichenbach, Experience and Prediction [OL70840W]
- Bradley, Appearance and Reality [OL3469495W], already flagged

## Rare sightings

Dretske's Knowledge and the Flow of Information [OL64359W] (borrowable) and Carnap's Der logische Aufbau der Welt [OL1176443W] are each logged by only a handful of readers.

## For this explorer

Four flags: Popper, Heidegger, Bradley and Pearl's Causality [OL4624596W] at BD541. Reichenbach is the obvious next step: free, about 410 pages, and about prediction itself. Popper's Objective Knowledge [OL1984562W] is borrowable, one shelf away from the flagged Conjectures.

## Lay of the land

Logic: 96 works. Special topics (BC171–199, 57 works) is the main town and holds argumentation and critical thinking at BC177; general works (BC60–99, 13) hold the classics. Probability, of the logical kind, has a small settlement at BC141.

## Landmarks

Mill's A System of Logic [OL1068214W] (114 editions), Boole's An Investigation of the Laws of Thought [OL2630376W] (82) and Couturat's L'algèbre de la logique [OL3871138W] (81).

## Free to forage

- Keynes, A Treatise on Probability [OL35949W], at BC141
- Boole, An Investigation of the Laws of Thought [OL2630376W]
- Whately, Elements of Logic [OL1128556W]

## Rare sightings

Stuart Russell's The Use of Knowledge in Analogy and Induction [OL2896992W] (borrowable) and Walton's Arguments from Ignorance [OL14852692W] are rarely logged; both treat inference under incomplete information.

## For this explorer

Three flags, including Mill. Keynes's Treatise is the strongest landfall on this coast: it is free, and its logical theory of probability is the counterpart to the Jaynes the explorer already holds in QA.
